## Projects

### EduScale
**Live:** https://eduscale.vercel.app/
**GitHub:** https://github.com/Shailesh93602/devscale
**Stack:** Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Prisma, PostgreSQL, Supabase, Socket.io, @socket.io/redis-adapter, redlock, opossum, prom-client, Bull, Redis, Node.js, Express.js

Engineering learning platform with a distributed real-time engine:

**Architecture:**
- `@socket.io/redis-adapter`: Socket.io cluster adapter for horizontal scaling across multiple Node.js instances. All instances share room state via Redis.
- `redlock` (Redlock algorithm): Distributed lock manager preventing race conditions when two users simultaneously attempt to start the same battle. The lock guards the battle start, submit-answer and complete handlers.
- `opossum`: Circuit breaker wrapping the remote code-execution service, with a transport timeout at or below the breaker's own deadline (`Backend/src/utils/deadlines.ts`) so a slow executor fails the submission fast rather than leaving the request hanging. The breaker is a single shared instance behind an unbounded per-user fan-out; `FINDINGS.md` §13 writes up why that is a design change rather than a timeout, and it is open.
- `prom-client`: Prometheus client exposing a `/metrics` endpoint with a request-duration histogram, an active-connection gauge and a memory gauge (plus Node default metrics).
- `bull` queues: background email delivery with a dead-letter queue for failed sends.
- `winston`: Structured logging with correlation IDs across distributed operations.

**Features:** Dynamic Career Roadmaps, real-time Battle Zone over Socket.io, multi-language code execution via Judge0, Community Forum, placement-preparation tracks, gamification.

### KhataGO
**Live:** https://khatago.vercel.app/
**Stack:** Next.js (App Router + API routes), TypeScript, Prisma, PostgreSQL (Supabase), Gemini AI (function-calling, 10 tools), WhatsApp Cloud API, i18next, Node.js worker process, Docker, promptproof (evals), LangGraph.js (comparison engine behind a flag), MongoDB (opt-in trace store)
**Note:** Source code is private.

WhatsApp-first AI accounting platform for Indian SMBs:

**Technical depth:**
- **WhatsApp webhook idempotency (no cache):** Meta delivers at least once. The WhatsApp message id is a unique column, so a duplicate insert fails at the database; processing then begins with a conditional UPDATE flipping aiStatus PENDING→PROCESSING only if it is still PENDING. Zero rows changed means another delivery already claimed it, so concurrent redeliveries produce exactly one Gemini run — and idempotency can never drift from the audit row the way a separate cache can. Asserted against a real Postgres: 8 simultaneous deliveries of one message collapse to one stored row; 8 concurrent executors of one agent write step commit exactly one ledger row.
- **Gemini AI OCR pipeline:** WhatsApp image URL → download to buffer → Gemini Vision API → structured JSON (merchant, amount, date, line items) → ledger transaction. Error handling for low-confidence extractions.
- **Tally XML export:** Generates TALLYMESSAGE XML vouchers for accountants. Non-trivial: Tally requires specific date format, ledger name lookup from master data, and precise GST field structure. Wrong XML silently fails to import.
- **Fast webhook ack + a worker over Postgres:** The handler persists the message and returns to Meta immediately. A containerized polling worker (a standalone Node process in the same Docker image as the web app) drains the queue — the Postgres table itself, claimed with an atomic conditional UPDATE, retried with exponential backoff and jitter (250ms → 30s), dead-lettered after 3 attempts, with an audited admin replay. No broker: the table already has visibility timeouts (`aiClaimedAt`) and attempt counts, and a second system whose state can disagree with the first would only add a failure mode.
- **Agent loop as a resumable state machine (in the repository, merged 2026-09-05, not yet deployed):** the model's plan for each turn is persisted before any tool runs; a write tool commits in the same transaction as its step, so a crash resumes from the last durable turn and at-most-once execution is a property of the database, not of control flow. Bring-your-own Gemini keys get per-key cooldown isolation. Each run is traced as one document (Postgres JSONB by default, a MongoDB adapter opt-in). 21 deterministic evals run in CI through promptproof under both the default loop and a LangGraph.js rendering behind a flag; retention crons bound traces, runs and steps.
- **i18next:** Full UI in English, Hindi, and Gujarati.

---

### CodeSenseiSearch
**GitHub:** https://github.com/Shailesh93602/CodeSenseiSearch
**Stack:** pnpm monorepo — Next.js 16 / React 19 front end, NestJS 11 API, TypeScript, Prisma 6, PostgreSQL + pgvector, BullMQ on Redis, Gemini embeddings, Docker Compose. Nothing is deployed: the repository runs locally.

AI-powered semantic code search engine. The pipeline is implemented end to end in the repository and has never been hosted:

**Architecture:**
- **Ingestion:** BullMQ queues on Redis → ContentChunkingWorker → AST-aware chunker that walks the TypeScript compiler API for .ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx (character-based fallback otherwise), one chunk per top-level function / method / class with real startLine / endLine
- **Embedding:** EmbeddingGenerationWorker → Gemini embeddings → vector(768) on content_chunks. Idempotent: only PENDING/FAILED chunks are claimed and the batch is flagged IN_PROGRESS before any network call, so concurrent workers cannot embed the same chunk. Exponential backoff on 429/5xx, immediate bail on 4xx.
- **Search:** Natural language query → embedding → hybrid ranking (pgvector cosine similarity + full-text + reranker) → ranked file+line results, behind JWT + GitHub OAuth with a global 60 req/min throttler
- **Key insight:** Chunking at function/class boundaries keeps semantic units intact. Fixed-size chunking splits logic mid-function, producing noisy embeddings.

**Not done, stated plainly:** no hosted deployment, and no integration test against a real Postgres — the end-to-end pipeline test runs in memory against a mocked embedder.

---

### BALLAST
**GitHub:** https://github.com/Shailesh93602/ballast
**Stack:** TypeScript (ESM, strict). Zero runtime dependencies; typescript, eslint, prettier, vitest and `pg` (the flash-sale arm) are dev-only.

Deterministic simulation of a multi-tenant session control plane — per-tenant parallel caps, a rolling credit/quota window, a finite pre-warmed capacity pool, leases over a substrate that lies, and an at-least-once completion channel as a durable replay log.

- **Determinism is the design, not a feature:** the whole execution is a pure function of one integer seed. 1,000 seeds replay byte-identically, in-process and across a fresh process, so any failure is reproducible from a single number.
- **Verified four independent ways:** 8 invariants checked after every event (2,000 histories), a model-based reference oracle run differentially against the implementation, mechanical mutation testing (161 of 167 mutants killed, 96.4%, over `src/policy`; 16 of 16 semantic mutants caught), and a shrinker that verifies its own reduction.
- **The ledger is the artifact:** `docs/LEDGER.md` lists 9 real findings nobody planted — and 4 of them were in the CHECKER, not the system under test (an invariant that trusted the plane's self-report, a reference that billed unspent credit, a harness that reported 100% on a red suite, a mutation operator that did not negate). Planted mutants live in `MUTATION.md` and are deliberately kept out of the ledger.
- **Semantics before code:** 38 ambiguities decided in writing before any policy code, with git history as proof the decisions were not written afterwards.
- **A flash-sale arm** measures three never-oversell strategies against a real PostgreSQL under 200 concurrent buyers, judged by counting rows rather than trusting any strategy's tally: read-then-write sold 200 of 5 units; conditional update and optimistic versioning each sold exactly 5, the latter paying 748 retries for it.

---

### Grounded — Production RAG Starter
**GitHub:** https://github.com/Shailesh93602/grounded
**Stack:** TypeScript, pgvector (behind a `VectorStore` interface), OpenAI or a local hash embedder, Vitest

A RAG starter that answers only from its sources, cites them, and refuses rather than hallucinating:
- **The refusal is a gate, not a prompt.** If the top retrieved chunk scores below `minScore`, the pipeline returns a fixed refusal with `grounded: false` and never calls the model. The system prompt says the same thing as defence in depth — a model can be talked out of an instruction, it cannot answer from context it was never given.
- **Idempotent ingestion:** chunks are content-hashed, so re-ingesting an unchanged document is a near no-op and deleted chunks are pruned.
- **Retry that fails fast on 4xx:** `isRetryable` retries connection errors, 429 and 5xx with jitter; a 400 or an auth failure fails immediately.
- 50 tests, 41 of which run with no database at all.

---

### idempotency-kit
**GitHub:** https://github.com/Shailesh93602/idempotency-kit
**Stack:** TypeScript, zero runtime dependencies, Vitest

The Stripe `Idempotency-Key` pattern as a library: an atomic claim so two simultaneous retries cannot both run the operation, replay of the stored result for the loser, release on transient failure so a legitimate retry is never poisoned, and a fingerprint-mismatch guard that rejects a key reused for a different request body. Waiting for the in-flight winner is opt-in (`waitRetries` / `waitIntervalMs`); the default is fail-fast. A sliding-window rate limiter sits on the same pluggable async store. 22 tests, fully offline.

---

### promptproof
**GitHub:** https://github.com/Shailesh93602/promptproof
**Stack:** TypeScript, zero runtime dependencies, Vitest

LLM eval and regression-diff kit: define cases, grade outputs, save a baseline, and fail CI on any pass-to-fail transition. Graders for exact match, includes, regex, JSON shape and token overlap, plus bring-your-own. KhataGO uses it to score its 21 deterministic evals in CI under both its own agent loop and a LangGraph.js engine. 27 tests, no API key needed to exercise the harness.
